papers.title_en: TRACE: Topology-Aware Reconnection via Prediction-Adaptive Connectivity Enforcement for Thin-Structure Segmentation
papers.evidence: 面向细长结构的拓扑感知分割
papers.tldr: 细长结构分割对局部错误极敏感，少量断点即可破坏整体连通性。TRACE提出预测自适应的拓扑感知目标，用目标骨架定义局部连接，并在当前预测下寻找最易重连路径联合监督瓶颈与骨架点。方法还引入保留前景及类别拓扑的骨架载体。在六个2D/3D基准上，TRACE提升连通性与拓扑质量，同时保持分割精度且训练开销低。
papers.abstract_en: Thin, elongated structures are particularly sensitive to connectivity errors, as even a few local segmentation mistakes can disrupt otherwise continuous paths. Existing skeleton-based objectives typically supervise fixed centerline locations and do not account for alternative local routes that may restore connectivity. We propose TRACE, a topology-aware, prediction-adaptive objective that uses a target skeleton to define required local connections. For each connection, TRACE identifies the easiest valid reconnection under the current prediction and jointly supervises its bottleneck with the corresponding skeleton point. The supervision thus adapts to the evolving prediction rather than remaining fixed to the centerline. We further introduce a topology-aware skeleton carrier that preserves both foreground and class-specific topology, enabling reliable definition of these connections. Extensive experiments across six 2D and 3D benchmarks show that TRACE improves connectivity and topology while maintaining strong segmentation accuracy with low training overhead. Code will be released upon acceptance.

papers.title_en: SCMerge: Spatial-Consistency-Aware Token Pair Merging for Efficient Semantic Segmentation
papers.authors: Junfeng Ren, Yi Gong, Yuan Zeng
papers.evidence: 面向语义分割Transformer的高效token合并
papers.tldr: ViT语义分割受二次注意力复杂度制约，现有token合并多依赖特征相似度而忽视空间一致性，易引入分割误差。SCMerge是一种免训练token合并方法，联合特征相似度与空间一致性配对token，在编码器内合并并在解码后重建到原patch网格。在ADE20K、Pascal Context和Cityscapes上，它比基线取得更优的精度-效率权衡，且可即插即用。
papers.abstract_en: Vision Transformer architectures have showcased impressive performance on semantic segmentation, yet their quadratic attention complexity hinders practical applications. Recent works have focused on merging tokens to reduce sequence length and thus improve transformer efficiency. However, existing token merging methods primarily rely on feature similarity to identify similar tokens, overlooking spatial consistency, which may introduce segmentation errors in semantic segmentation. In this work, we propose SCMerge, a training-free token merging method that jointly considers feature similarity and spatial consistency in pairing similar tokens. The pairwise tokens are then merged within the encoder, and the resulting token sequences are reconstructed onto the original patch grid after decoding. The proposed method is flexible and can be plugged into existing vision Transformer-based semantic segmentation pipelines. Extensive experiments on the benchmark datasets ADE20K, Pascal Context, and Cityscapes show that SCMerge consistently achieves a better trade-off between segmentation accuracy and efficiency than baseline methods.

papers.title_en: VesperMUSE: Multi-Modal Fusion Vision Transformer for Image Semantic Segmentation Under Diverse Light Conditions
papers.evidence: 多模态视觉Transformer实现鲁棒语义分割
papers.tldr: 低光照下语义分割因噪声、伪影、颜色失真和结构细节丢失而显著退化，影响自动驾驶等系统的可靠感知。VesperMUSE提出统一多模态框架：先用物理启发的合成低光适配算法，再以热成像引导低光增强，最后动态融合RGB、热成像与表面法线图。核心是可扩展、与模态无关的自注意力，可处理任意数量辅助输入且无需改架构。实验表明其能恢复缺失视觉线索，在极端非结构化环境中达到SOTA。
papers.abstract_en: Semantic segmentation is critical for the reliable navigation and scene understanding of autonomous systems, yet its performance degrades severely in low-light environments due to noise, artifacts, colour distortion, and the loss of structural details. To address this challenge, this work introduces VesperMUSE, a unified multi-modal framework designed to achieve robust image semantic segmentation across diverse illumination conditions. The architecture addresses the light deficiency problem on multiple levels: proposing a novel physics-informed synthetic low-light adaptation algorithm, approaching Low-Light Image Enhancement (LLIE) through a thermal-guided paradigm, and finally aiming to recover the intrinsic scene details for semantic segmentation through a multi-modal fusion approach. Following enhancement, the framework dynamically integrates the primary RGB features with auxiliary thermal representations and surface normal maps highlighting geometric discontinuities and material boundaries. At the core of this integration is a highly scalable, modality-agnostic self-attention mechanism that extracts both global context and fine local features from an arbitrary number of auxiliary inputs. By combining and projecting these hierarchical multi-modal representations into a unified component, the attention module allows the network to selectively attend to relevant cross-modal cues without requiring any architectural modifications when different sensor configurations are used. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that VesperMUSE successfully recovers missing visual cues, providing a flexible, state-of-the-art (SOTA) solution for machine perception in extreme and unstructured real-world environments.
